newsitem.title: USA: U.S. LPG markets slow after busy start to '97.
newsitem.headline: U.S. LPG markets slow after busy start to '97.

text.p: U.S. liquified petroleum gas (LPG) prices were mixed, staging a recovery from earlier losses Friday but in a slow session after Thursday's busy start to the year.
The January 2nd session was a volatile one which saw prompt propane prices at the MidWest hub at Conway, Kansas trade a 10-cent range and end up on the day either side of 70 cents a gallon.
Propane at Conway was at about 67/68 cents on Friday, though prices at the Belvieu, Texas hub moved up a couple of cents late in the session to trade last at about 52 cents a gallon.
"Sometimes the first (business day) of the month can be that way but today nobody has been calling," said a major LPG producer in Texas.

The freeze in Europe wasn't drawing in product from the U.S. because of high shipping costs so U.S. prices were being hit in the last couple of weeks by the big thaw this side of the Atlantic, brokers and traders said.

"Any ships that do firm up with January (bill of lading dates) run the risk of double exposure," said a Houston broker. The high shipping costs to Europe and the risk that Saudi February prices may slam the market on the return trip are too risky to entice business, the broker said.

Meanwhile, some late business firmed ethane prices and deals were done around 35.5/36 cents/gallon for Belvieu delivery. A natural gasoline deal for Warren delivery at 62.25 cents pegged Belvieu at either side of 62 cents, market players said.
-- Tony McAuley, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1623
